result.description:
Lead mechanical capital projects from design to commissioning while enjoying a 5:2 roster   Your new company    Our client is a leading Australian resources organisation with a strong focus on operational excellence, innovation, and sustainable growth. With significant investment in asset upgrades and infrastructure improvements, they offer the opportunity to work on challenging and rewarding projects within a supportive and high-performing team. 
   Your new role    As a Mechanical Project Manager, you will be responsible for delivering a portfolio of mechanical capital projects from concept through to commissioning and handover. Working closely with engineering consultants, contractors, operations teams, and key stakeholders, you will ensure projects are delivered safely, efficiently, and in line with business objectives. 
 Key responsibilities include: 
 
 Managing mechanical projects through all phases of the project life cycle 
 Coordinating consultants during scoping, study, and detailed design stages 
 Managing project schedules, budgets, risks, and reporting requirements 
 Overseeing contractor performance and ensuring contractual obligations are met 
 Leading project execution, construction activities, commissioning, and handover 
 Ensuring project documentation is maintained and complies with governance requirements 
 Collaborating with maintenance, operations, engineering, and site leadership teams 
 Monitoring project performance and driving continuous improvement initiatives 
 Ensuring all works are completed in accordance with safety, quality, and environmental standards 
 
   What you'll need to succeed  
 
 Demonstrated experience managing mechanical projects within mining, resources, heavy industry, manufacturing, or infrastructure environments 
 Proven experience managing consultants through early study and detailed design phases 
 Experience delivering projects through execution, construction, and commissioning 
 Strong understanding of project governance, project controls, and delivery documentation 
 Sound knowledge of contract administration and contractor management 
 Strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills 
 Ability to manage multiple project priorities in a fast-paced operational environment 
 Mechanical Engineering qualifications or a Mechanical Trade background will be highly regarded. 
 Commitment to maintaining high safety and operational standards 
 
   What you'll get in return  
 This is an exciting opportunity to join a leading mining operation and play a key role in the delivery of critical mechanical infrastructure and asset improvement projects. You'll enjoy a Monday-to-Thursday site-based roster with the flexibility to work from home on Fridays, camp accommodation provided, and the choice of FIFO or DIDO arrangements. Working within a collaborative and experienced project team, you'll have the opportunity to make a tangible impact while further developing your project management career in a dynamic mining environment. 
   What you need to do now  
 If you're interested in this role, applications can be submitted via the "apply now" button. Please ensure you are submitting an up-to-date CV. If you have any further questions, please call Jennah Murray 07 4960 1129. 
   
 If this job isn't quite right for you, but you are looking for a new position, please contact us for a confidential discussion about your career.  Please  click here  to apply.

result.description:
Our Company

TerraCom Limited (ASX: TER) is an Australian based mining resources company with a global footprint, comprising a large portfolio of operating assets in Australia and South Africa within the coal sectors. We are a renowned low-cost producer focused on delivering exceptional outcomes from our high yielding diversified asset portfolio for its investors. TerraCom owns and operates the Blair Athol Coal Mine, in Central Queensland. This open-cut thermal coal operation consists of a full suite of mining activities inclusive of dragline, truck and excavator, dozer push, mine site rehabilitation, coal processing, coal crushing, product haulage and train load-out activities.

The Blair Athol Coal mine is located 24km northwest of the family-friendly township of Clermont in Central Queensland, 120 km northwest of Emerald and 275km southwest of Mackay.

TerraCom supports our people to grow, learn and develop their skills to reach their potential. We offer an exciting working environment, with career progression opportunities, as we truly believe that the capability and performance of our people is key to our success. Blair Athol Mine believes in fostering and nurturing each of our team members by providing them with a safe and enjoyable place to work, along with guidance and support from a leader they can rely upon. Come and play a key role in shaping our future!

The Role

We are currently seeking a highly motivated Surveyor Assistant / Technician to join our team at Blair Athol. You will assist the Surveyor in providing support for survey control to facilitate execution of mine activities including topsoil, stripping, overburden removal, coal mining, drilling/blasting, rehabilitation and associated projects around the mine. The right candidate will also forge a pathway towards further qualifications within the mine engineering team.

Responsibilities of the Role will include:

* Provide survey services and set out control points to ensure the accurate location and layout of work within the limits, offsets, grades, profiles and elevations for all mining related processes in accordance with the mine design criteria
* Conduct survey operations with drones, laser scanners and GPS and process the data to meet the required schedules
* Process survey data accurately and complete volume quantities
* Measure distances, angles and variations across site as directed
* Identify & escalate any non-conformance or processes that require corrective action.

Skills and Experience:

* A good work ethic, great communication skills and a desire to learn and grow
* A strong commitment to safety
* Survey or operational experience within a civil or mining environment
* Ability to prioritise and schedule work
* Ability to accurately measure and interpret data
* Competent user of MS Office tools

Benefits

* A fantastic opportunity to expand your mining career and join a great team offering exposure to all areas of operations and become part of the community in which you work.
* An attractive remuneration package in line with experience.
* An inclusive and supportive team culture.
* Excellent opportunity for career development

Note we thank all applicants for their interest, however any communications will be with short listed candidates only. No agency applications accepted.

Diamond Quality Cabinets delivers the finest architecturally designed cabinets in Mackay, adding functionality and style to your home or business. By taking your budget, tastes and preferences into account, we create ideal cabinetry and wardrobe solutions to suit a range of applications.

From high-end custom kitchens and exclusive master closets to elegant libraries and unique home theatres, we are capable of turning your vision into a reality. Let us define your environment, enrich your living space and increase the value of your property with our timeless installations. Our in-house interior design team will also help with the selection of colours, countertop materials and the placement of your cabinets.

We have years of experience renovating kitchens and bathrooms, building and remodelling homes, and updating commercial spaces. During this time, we’ve built a reputation for solving problems creatively and thinking outside the box. You can bet we’ll get the job done quickly and efficiently.

We are seeking highly skilled Cabinet Makers to join our dedicated team of professionals.

As a Cabinet Maker you will fabricate, assemble, repair, and install custom wooden cabinetry, counters, and furniture. Interpret blueprints, operate woodworking machinery, and assemble components with precise hardware. The work involves selecting materials, applying finishes, and ensuring the final product meets both aesthetic and functional requirements.

The role includes but is not limited to:
Study blueprints, sketches, and work orders to determine specifications to create custom cabinet, counters, and furniture
Choose appropriate materials such as timbers, plywoods, veneers, particle board, synthetic wood, and other engineered wood products and estimate the total costs of the materials
Plan an effective approach to work to ensure that each project is completed on time
Cuts, shapes and assembles materials to build cabinetry and fittings
Utilise and control CAD and CNC machines to precisely mark out, cut and shape components
Apply finishes to cabinetry and fittings for aesthetics
Apply protective coatings to cabinets and furniture fitting hinges, locks, catches, drawers, shelves and other associated hardware
Collaborate with clients and tradespeople for accurate installation
Install cabinetry and fittings in various areas as directed
Repair or refurbish damaged cabinetry and fittings

To be considered for this role, you must have the following:
Trade qualified with proven experience in the same field
Knowledge in operating wide range of hand tools and power tools
Strong attention to detail and the ability to conduct quality checks on completed work
Ability to meet tight deadlines without sacrificing workmanship
Ability to work independently or as part of a team to complete assigned tasks
Knowledge of safety procedures and regulations to prevent accidents and injuries in the workplace
Physically fit and able to lift large, heavy equipment and materials
Attention to detail
Strong communication skills
Excellent reporting skills
Self-motivated, organised, punctual and reliable
Must have great work ethics

If you meet the above criteria and would like to be considered for this position, please apply now!
Salary: Between $79,499 and $82,000 per annum + Super

Job Description:
The Analyst Programmer is responsible for designing, developing, testing, and maintaining software applications that support business objectives. Key duties include writing and reviewing code, conducting software testing, and ensuring that application functionality meets specified requirements. The role also involves researching and designing technical solutions, as well as documenting and updating software specifications throughout the development lifecycle.
Responsibilities:
Demonstrate a strong understanding of coding methods, industry best practices, and software development standards.
Conduct interviews with end-users to gather insights into functionality, interface issues, usability, and challenges, ensuring user needs are effectively addressed.
Develop comprehensive test cases and test plans to ensure the reliability and performance of software applications.
Stay informed on data privacy laws and practices to ensure software development remains compliant.
Communicate clearly with non-technical staff and collaborate effectively across multidisciplinary teams.
Embrace new technologies and maintain a commitment to ongoing learning and skill development.
Display excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills to convey ideas and requirements effectively.
Conduct research into software-related challenges and assess potential solutions or products.
Demonstrate initiative, autonomy, and direction in executing work tasks and delivering projects.
Maintain strong attention to detail, ensuring accuracy and precision throughout the development process.
Apply analytical and problem-solving skills to resolve complex software-related issues.
Manage task prioritisation and execute effectively under pressure to meet project deadlines.
Collaborate closely with developers, programmers, and designers to conceptualise and develop innovative software solutions.
Evaluate existing business systems and processes to identify optimisation opportunities.
Assist in gathering, defining, and documenting business requirements, deliverables, and specifications in partnership with internal departments.
Contribute to software development project planning, including scope definition, scheduling, and implementation.
Engage with internal and external programme users to understand and fulfil functional requirements.
Qualifications:
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a closely related discipline.
At least 2 years of hands-on experience working as an Analyst Programmer or in a similar software development role.
Proficient in one or more programming languages such as Java, C#, Python, or JavaScript.
Strong understanding of database concepts and practical experience writing and optimising SQL queries.
Experience developing web applications using technologies such as HTML, CSS, JavaScript, React, Angular, or ASP.NET.
Familiarity with modern software development methodologies, including Agile and Scrum frameworks.
Sound knowledge of software testing principles, with exposure to tools like JUnit or Selenium.
Experience using version control systems such as Git or SVN, and project tracking tools like JIRA or Trello.
Understanding of cloud platforms such as AWS or Azure, along with their core services and deployment models.
Solid foundation in object-oriented programming (OOP) and commonly used software design patterns.
Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills, with the ability to identify and resolve complex coding issues.
Effective communicator with the ability to collaborate across multidisciplinary teams and stakeholders.
Demonstrated ability to manage tasks, prioritise deliverables, and meet project deadlines.
Self-motivated with a commitment to ongoing learning and staying current with emerging tools and technologies.
Permanent Residents (PR) and Australian Citizens are eligible to apply
Job Types: Full-time, Permanent
Salary: $70,000 – $120,000 per year + Super
Benefits: Work from home
Schedule: 8-hour shift
Work Authorisation: Australia (Required)

result.description: AGROVISE  Due to continued business growth, we are seeking a motivated and experienced Agricultural and Agritech Technician to join our team. The successful applicant will support the installation, commissioning, operation, testing, maintenance and optimisation of agricultural technology systems and equipment, while assisting with irrigation management, precision agriculture, crop production technologies, field trials, technical data collection and the delivery of innovative agritech solutions across a range of agricultural projects in Western Australia.   Benefits   Competitive salary package of $80,000 – $100,000 plus superannuation.   Ongoing training and professional development in agricultural technology, irrigation and automation systems.   Opportunity to work with innovative agricultural, water and renewable energy projects across Western Australia.    Task & responsibilities   Examine topographical, physical and soil characteristics of farmland to assist in determining optimal land use and identifying nutrient deficiencies.   Assist Agricultural Research Scientists and Agronomists in developing improved methods of planting, fertilising, irrigation, harvesting and crop management to maximise productivity.   Identify plant diseases, pests, fungi and weeds affecting agricultural production and assist in implementing appropriate control measures.   Provide technical advice, training and support to clients on agricultural technology solutions, including sensors, remote monitoring systems, farm management software and automation technologies.   Install, configure, program, test, commission, repair and maintain advanced agricultural technology and equipment, including irrigation controllers, pumping systems, sensors, telemetry, automation and precision agriculture systems.   Develop, operate and maintain integrated agricultural technology systems used in irrigation, water management and farm production, including analysing operational data and preparing technical reports.   Conduct field testing, equipment inspections, fault diagnosis and preventative maintenance to ensure efficient operation of agricultural infrastructure and agritech equipment.   Collect, record and analyse technical and operational data to evaluate system performance and recommend improvements.   Prepare technical documentation, maintenance records, installation reports and service schedules.   Work collaboratively with engineers, project managers and clients to deliver innovative agricultural infrastructure and technology solutions while ensuring compliance with workplace health and safety requirements.    Qualification & experience   Certificate IV, Diploma or higher qualification in Agricultural Technology, Agricultural Engineering,  or a closely related discipline.   At least one year of relevant industry experience (more experienced applicants are encouraged to apply).   Experience working with irrigation systems, pumps, agricultural equipment or automated control systems.    About Company    Agrovise is a Western Australian engineering and agritech company specialising in greenhouse infrastructure, protected cropping and agricultural technology solutions. The company designs, installs and maintains greenhouse systems, irrigation and fertigation infrastructure, climate control and automation systems, helping commercial growers improve productivity, water efficiency and sustainable farming practices across Western Australia. result.description:
Lead electrical mining projects from concept to commissioning while enjoying a 5:2 roster   Your new company  
 Our client is a leading Australian resources organisation with a strong commitment to operational excellence, safety, and sustainable project delivery. With a substantial portfolio of capital projects and ongoing investment in site infrastructure, they offer the opportunity to work on complex projects within a collaborative and high-performing team environment. 
   Your new role  
 As an Electrical Project Manager, you will be responsible for managing electrical capital projects through the full project life cycle, from early studies and detailed design through to construction, commissioning, and handover. You will work closely with consultants, contractors, and key stakeholders to deliver projects safely, on schedule, and within budget. 
 Key responsibilities include: 
 
 Managing electrical projects from concept development through to completion 
 Coordinating consultants during feasibility studies, engineering, and detailed design phases 
 Managing project budgets, schedules, risks, and reporting requirements 
 Overseeing contractors and ensuring compliance with contractual obligations 
 Leading project execution, construction activities, and commissioning works 
 Reviewing and managing project documentation, technical deliverables, and governance requirements 
 Collaborating with operations, maintenance, engineering, and external stakeholders 
 Ensuring all work is delivered in line with safety, quality, and regulatory requirements 
 Driving project performance and continuous improvement outcomes 
 
   What you'll need to succeed     
 
 Demonstrated experience managing electrical projects within mining, resources, heavy industry, energy, or infrastructure environments 
 Proven experience managing consultants through study, design, and project delivery phases 
 Strong understanding of project delivery methodologies and project governance requirements 
 Experience managing contractors during construction and commissioning activities 
 Sound knowledge of contract administration and contractor management 
 Strong stakeholder engagement, communication, and leadership skills 
 Ability to manage multiple project priorities in a dynamic operational environment 
 Electrical trade or engineering qualifications will be highly regarded. 
 Commitment to maintaining the highest safety standards 
 
   What you'll get in return  
 This is an excellent opportunity to join a highly regarded mining operation and contribute to the successful delivery of critical electrical infrastructure projects. You'll work on a Monday-to-Thursday site roster with the flexibility to work from home on Fridays, while camp accommodation is provided throughout your assignment. Both FIFO and DIDO options are available, offering flexibility for candidates across Queensland. You'll join a supportive team environment where your expertise will directly influence the success of key site projects and future growth initiatives. 
   What you need to do now  
 If you're interested in this role, applications can be submitted via the "apply now" button. Please ensure you are submitting an up-to-date CV. If you have any further questions, please call Jennah Murray 07 4960 1129. 
   
 If this job isn't quite right for you, but you are looking for a new position, please contact us for a confidential discussion about your career.  Please  click here  to apply.

Position: Construction Project Manager
Position Type: Full Time
Salary: $110,000 - $130,000 p.a plus Super
Employer Name: J & DE HOMES PTY LTD - T/a JDE HOMES
A.B.N. 24 614 743 789
Job Location: Level 2, 207 Pulteney Street, Adelaide, SA, 5000,  AUSTRALIA
Advertising Period: 28 days - 13 Jul 2026 > 10 Aug 2026

Please include Reference: J1697-Workforce in the Subject Line and email all applications and CV to apply@jobsource.net.au

Summary

Our client JDE Homes is seeking to add a Construction Project Manager to its South Australian construction and development team. The company delivers fixed-price property construction, development and project management services across residential, civil, industrial and commercial projects. This role will support the planning, coordination and delivery of technically challenging building projects, while maintaining quality, budget, safety and completion requirements.

The typical job responsibilities will include, but are not limited to the following:

- Plan, organise and manage construction projects from commencement through to practical completion.
- Coordinate project resources, including labour, subcontractors, materials, plant and equipment.
- Interpret architectural drawings, construction plans, engineering details and technical specifications.
- Monitor project budgets, timelines, quality standards, risks and contractual obligations.
- Liaise with architects, engineers, consultants, clients, subcontractors and relevant authorities.
- Manage procurement scheduling and ensure materials are available to meet construction milestones.
- Supervise site progress and ensure works align with approved plans and specifications.
- Coordinate inspections, approvals and documentation required by councils and regulatory bodies.
- Ensure adherence to workplace health, safety, building and performance standards.
- Negotiate with suppliers, subcontractors and stakeholders throughout the project lifecycle.
- Prepare project reports, progress updates, cost reviews and construction documentation.
- Manage project variations, delays, defects and implementation of corrective actions.
- Lead subcontractors and site teams to achieve quality and programme outcomes.
- Support tender preparation, contract administration and construction methodology recommendations.
- Maintain professional communication with clients to support cost-effective project delivery.

Applicants must meet the following minimum requirements to be considered for the role:

- Minimum ten years of relevant experience in construction project management or building project delivery.
- Strong ability to manage residential, commercial, civil or industrial construction projects from start to finish.
- Demonstrated experience coordinating subcontractors, trades, consultants, suppliers, plant, equipment and site resources.
- Sound knowledge of construction drawings, specifications, building processes, safety obligations and quality standards.
- Proven ability to monitor project costs, budgets, schedules, risks, variations and completion deadlines.
- Strong communication skills for liaising with clients, architects, engineers, authorities and internal project teams.
- Practical experience resolving construction issues and recommending cost-effective building methods or project solutions.
- Ability to work without direct supervision while maintaining accurate project records and professional standards.

Please include Reference: J1697-Workforce in the Subject Line and email all applications and CV to apply@jobsource.net.au

Due to the volume of applicants, only those meeting the minimum standards will be considered and only successful applicants will be contacted.  Thank you for your interest in the role.

Maintenance Fitter - South Nowra, NSW 
   
 Full-Time Permanent Opportunity | Food Manufacturing | Up to $40/hr base rate + shift loading + Super 
   
 Hays are currently partnering with a well-established food manufacturing business in South Nowra to recruit an experienced Maintenance Fitter to join their Engineering team. 
 This is an excellent opportunity for a trade-qualified fitter who enjoys a hands-on role, working across preventative maintenance, breakdown response, equipment upgrades and continuous improvement projects within a fast-paced production environment. 
 About the Role 
 Reporting to the Engineering Manager, you will join a close-knit maintenance team consisting of Maintenance Fitters and a Maintenance Manager who oversees day-to-day operations. 
 Working across rotating shifts, you'll play a key role in ensuring production equipment operates safely and efficiently while supporting the installation and commissioning of a new manufacturing line. 
   
 Hours: 
 
 Full-time permanent position 
 37.5 hours per week 
 Rotating shifts:
 
 6:00am - 2:00pm 
 11:00am - 7:00pm 
 
 
 Flexibility to work both shifts is essential, although afternoon-focused arrangements may be considered following successful training. 
 
 Key Responsibilities 
 
 Carry out preventative and scheduled maintenance on manufacturing equipment 
 Respond to machinery breakdowns, faults, jams and equipment failures 
 Troubleshoot and repair mechanical systems to minimise downtime 
 Assist with machinery installations, upgrades and improvement projects 
 Support the commissioning of a new gummies production line 
 Ensure machinery and components meet Australian safety standards 
 Maintain accurate maintenance records and documentation 
 Promote and follow all workplace safety, GMP and food safety procedures 
 
 About You 
 To be successful in this role, you will have: 
 
 Trade qualification as a Mechanical Fitter or Maintenance Fitter 
 Previous experience working within a manufacturing environment 
 Strong fault-finding and breakdown maintenance capability 
 Experience with preventative maintenance programmes 
 Ability to work both independently and as part of a team 
 Commitment to workplace safety and continuous improvement 
 
 Highly Desirable 
 
 Food manufacturing experience 
 Understanding of GMP (Good Manufacturing Practices) 
 Exposure to food safety and quality systems 
 Experience working with automated production equipment 
 Experience commissioning or installing new machinery 
 
 What's on Offer? 
 
 Permanent full-time employment 
 Competitive hourly rate up to $40 per hour + superannuation 
 Stable Monday to Friday roster 
 Opportunity to work on new production line installations 
 Supportive engineering team and leadership 
 Long-term career growth with a successful manufacturing business 
 
     If you're interested in this role, click 'apply now' to forward an up-to-date copy of your CV to David.lynes@hays.com.au, or call Dave on 0477551369 now. The role involves interpreting engineering drawings, manufacturing and assembling metal parts, and delivering precision repairs to support RiteBore's onsite lineboring and heavy machinery services.   Key Responsibilities    Fabricate, assemble and repair metal components and structures used in heavy machinery and industrial equipment.   Operate and maintain ELSA Supercombinata lineboring equipment, facing head and computerised ELSA bore welding system.  Interpret engineering drawings, blueprints and specifications to determine fabrication requirements.   Mark out, cut, shape and form structural steel and metal components using hand tools, power tools and fabrication equipment.   Perform welding using MIG & Bore welder welding techniques to manufacture and repair heavy equipment components.   Carry out line boring preparation, hard facing, gouging and associated fabrication works.  Fit fabricated metal components and ensure correct alignment and tolerances.   Inspect completed fabrication work to ensure compliance with engineering specifications and quality standards.   Perform maintenance and repairs on buckets, booms, pins, bushes, agricultural machinery and earthmoving equipment.   Operate fabrication machinery including presses, grinders, drills, cutting equipment and other workshop machinery safely and efficiently.   Maintain a safe, clean and organised work environment while complying with workplace health and safety procedures.    What We’re Looking For    At least 3 Years of experience operating lineboring equipment.  Supplier approved training Certificate for ELSA lineboring equipment (Highly recommended).  Knowledge and experience on Elsa line boring machines (Highly Recommended).   Australian Recognised Fitter/Welder Trade Certificate (Fitter & welder).  Experience in overlay welding.  Machining of Faces and Flanges.  Demonstrated experience in lineboring welding machine maintenance, repairing components for machinery such as CAT, Liebherr, Sandvik equipment, Hitachi, Komatsu(Velmet), John Deere and Tiger cat.  Display a clear commitment and focus on the health, safety, and well-being of all employees.  Strong interpersonal and communication skills.  Hold a valid Australian Drivers Licence.  Willingness to undertake a Pre-Employment Medical & Drug/Alcohol Screen.      About Company    RiteBore is a small, family-owned, onsite lineboring and welding business based in Bunbury, Western Australia. We  provide onsite Lineboring & Welding, Maintenance, Fitting & Field Service on Agricultural & Earthmoving Equipment  throughout Western Australia, supporting the mining and earthmoving industry.
